title: What is known about 1RB0RC_1LC0RB_1RE1LD_0LB0LF_---0RA_1LB1LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_1LC0RB_1RE1LD_0LB0LF_---0RA_1LB1LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Sweeps back and forth over a period-7 background (0101101 and its rightward form 1010100); a clean zone of it at the left end grows steadily, the rest is a soup of (10)^k, 010, 1 1 0 pieces; a halt needs E to read 1100. Lean proves the sweep rules over the background words and the only local pattern that leads to a halt; no halt in 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 56,258 cells have been visited and 27,701 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).

claims.title: The sweeps cross the background words whole
claims.text: 16 shift rules: for every n and every surrounding tape, a sweep in the stated state crosses n copies of a background word and leaves n copies of its partner, in the stated number of steps (for example L C> (0101101)^n R ⟶ L (1010100)^n C> R).

claims.title: The only way to a halt
claims.text: The machine halts only when E reads a 0, and the only way there is E reading 1 1 0 0 (E, A and C step right and E meets the last 0.

claims.title: What the tape looks like
claims.text: At the left end there is a clean zone of the period-7 word that grows steadily ((1010110)362 after 2·107 steps); the rest of the tape is a soup of (10)k, 1 1 0 1, (010)k and short pieces.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No invariant forbidding 1 1 0 0 under E is known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. Sweeps back and forth over a period-7 background (0101101 and its rightward form 1010100); a clean zone of it at the left end grows steadily, the rest is a soup of (10)^k, 010, 1 1 0 pieces; a halt needs E to read 1100. This page runs the real machine, explains its sweeps and the words they rewrite, and lists what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 56,258 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499).
After 109 steps the tape spans 56,258 cells (18,066 left of the start, 23,351 right), with a density of 1s of 0.492.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite a periodic tape
html: Rightward, C, E, A and B cross the period-7 word whole (9 steps a copy): C turns 0101101 into 1010100, E turns 1011010 into 0101001, and so on; on period 3 B turns 100 into 101 and A turns 010 into 110. Leftward, B, C and D take them back (23 or 25 steps a copy).
At the left end there is a clean zone of the period-7 word that grows steadily ((1010110)362 after 2·107 steps); the rest of the tape is a soup of (10)k, 1 1 0 1, (010)k and short pieces.

sections.heading: What one sweep does to the words it crosses
html: A shift rule says that a sweep crosses any number n of copies of a word in one state and leaves n copies of another word behind. These are proved in Lean for every n and every tape around them (lean/Rules.lean); S> is the head in state S on the next cell, L and R the rest of the tape.

sections.heading: The one pattern that halts, and why it has not appeared
html: The machine halts only when E reads a 0, and Lean proves that the only way there is E reading 1 1 0 0 (E, A and C step right and E meets the last 0; halt_needs_pattern, lean/Halt.lean). In 109 steps E read 1 1 0 followed by a 1 about 4·107 times, so the safety rests on the cell after 1 1 0.
No invariant forbidding 1 1 0 0 under E is known.
Next step. Find the block structure of the soup and the round-trip map on it.
